articles.title: Hexham polar explorer on his love of hen harriers and owls
articles.summary: Conrad Dickinson has travelled to the world's most remote places but loves photographing birds back home.
articles.body:
As a polar explorer, Conrad Dickinson has found himself face-to-face with arctic wolves and even got the chance to photograph polar bears, arctic foxes and other amazing wildlife.

Yet, he still loves to spend hours in the moorlands of his native North East and nearby Cumbria, patiently waiting to catch a glimpse of a hen harrier or a short-eared owl.

"Very often with bird photography, it involves hundreds if not thousands of hours sitting just waiting when nothing happens," says the 71-year-old from Hexham.

"Because there's lots of failed attempts, when you get that magic shot, it's a great feeling."

The North East is an excellent place to capture migratory birds along the coast, Dickinson says, as well as owls on the moorlands.

He says short-eared owls are one of the few species of owls that come out during the day, meaning they are easier to spot for non-experts.

"It depends on the vole population as to how many short-eared owls there are, and this year has been fantastic in Teesdale, Weardale, Northumberland, Cumbria - there's been quite a good number of short-eared owls."

Dickinson recently won a prize for his impressive shots of hen harriers , which can be seen at one of his favourite spots at RSPB Geltsdale, near Brampton, Cumbria.

"They're just such graceful fliers, hunting over the moors," Dickinson says.

As a RSPB volunteer, Dickinson has been monitoring hen harrier nests for 10 years and knows how and when best to capture them.

Using a long lens so not to disturb them, he says it is a thrill to catch them in all their majesty.

"The most magical thing that happens with the hen harriers is what's called a food pass," he explains.

The male goes hunting during nesting season and brings prey - generally a vole or small bird - back to the nest.

When the male returns, he drops the prey for the female who catches it mid-air.

"That's the real shot you want to try and get, but it's quite hard to capture," says Dickinson.

He was brought up in a rural farming community, the son of gamekeepers.

"I was always immersed in rural Northumberland and that worked hand in hand with wildlife and you just get to love wildlife and then the more you see, the more you want to see," he says.

The RSPB, which has called for greater protection of hen harriers, said the bird continued to be "illegally killed" in connection with land managed for driven grouse shooting.

Dickinson says they are "the most persecuted bird in England", but because of his background he thinks there is scope for collaboration to protect the birds.

"It's not all black and white, there's quite a bit of compromise. And it would be fantastic if both the sport shooting industry and the conservation industry can work in tandem, so that would be the ideal situation."

Hen harriers are fairly rare because of these challenges but they are not the most uncommon animal Dickinson has ever captured.

He specialised in arctic warfare when he was in the British Army, a task he says he found "quite easy", which led to a love of this unusual part of the world and an opportunity to work there.

He says: "You do some expeditions, then you do some more and then you do the hard ones and somebody invites you to be, I suppose, a polar guide and you get your qualifications and you take interesting people to cold places."

One memory that he says will stick with him forever was when he took two people from the North East to the remote Ellesmere Island, being followed by arctic wolves for three days.

"These wolves haven't seen people before so they're just curious and they come within 10 yards of you and it's a bit spooky at first, because they're big animals and they can be ferocious," he recalls.

He says the experience was "incredibly exciting" and a "real highlight", though the creature's curiosity "slightly wears you down after being there three days, three nights, following every movement".

Dickinson says he is as committed as ever to conservation and back on home turf he is the president of the Northumberland Wildlife Trust.

The charity is currently in the process of buying the Rothbury estate , a 3,800 hectare (15-sq-m) piece of land in Northumberland, where they plan to boost wildlife, restore bogs and promote nature-friendly farming on the site.

He says the organisation, which is close to raising the £30m it needs, is embedded in the territory and is committed to its preservation.

"We'll keep running it for the benefit of regenerative farming, we've got tenants that will remain and we'll also preserve it for the future for wildlife."

articles.title: Bengaluru sees flooded roads, fallen trees & traffic snarls
articles.summary: Heavy evening rain and strong winds flooded Bengaluru roads, toppled trees and snarled traffic; waterlogging hit Hebbal, Peenya, Whitefield and more.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A spell of heavy evening rain brought parts of Bengaluru to a standstill Wednesday, flooding roads, choking traffic and leaving motorists battling waterlogged stretches across several parts of the city.The downpour, accompanied by strong winds, brought down trees at multiple locations, further disrupting evening peak-hour traffic. India Meteorological Department (IMD) officials said the city received 1.6mm of rainfall until 8.30pm. “However, rain was intense in eastern parts of the city -- over 18mm,” an official said. According to KSNDMC, however, Bengaluru received an average of 10mm rainfall.The city was overcast since morning, but rain intensified towards evening, quickly turning several arterial roads, underpasses and low-lying stretches into waterlogged corridors. Peenya flyover, Hebbal Ring Road and several underpasses were among the worst affected. Water accumulated near Hebbal Ring Road, triggering long queues of vehicles.Commuters reported waterlogging near Hoodi Metro station. Varun Rao, a commuter, posted on X that there were hardly any drains between the Metro station and Hoodi circle, resulting in rainwater flowing directly onto the main road. He said pedestrians were forced to wade through ankle- to knee-deep water.Vidyashilp railway underpass in Yelahanka, Rashtrothana flyover, Choudappa Layout and Thanisandra Road were inundated, throwing traffic out of gear. A large tree was uprooted near Vijnana Nagar, bringing traffic towards Kaggadasapura to a halt. Another tree reportedly fell near Vidhya Soudha School, adding to the evening chaos. Water stagnated along the stretch from Rainbow Hospital towards Karthik Nagar, between Yelahanka BSF and Airport Road, and from Mahadevapura towards Lorry Junction, making commuting difficult.Similar scenes were reported on Vibgyor Road in Whitefield, where waterlogging left vehicles stranded and some motorists struggling to negotiate the flooded stretch. Sahakara Nagar too witnessed significant water accumulation, with clogged drains leaving roads inundated. articles.title: Why ‘kaun se wale papa’ remark led to man’s conviction
articles.summary: Delhi court convicts man under IPC 509 for saying “Kaun se wale papa?” to a woman, ruling it implied multiple partners and insulted her modesty.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark, “Kaun se wale papa?”, made when she told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Though the two had no prior dispute, the court held that the remark implied the woman had multiple partners and questioned the child’s paternity.Judicial magistrate first class Moksha Bains, in a Sept 24 judgment, said the remark was not an innocuous inquiry about the child’s father but carried an insinuation about the woman’s sexual propriety and fidelity. “The expression, when addressed to a woman in the aforesaid setting, is not an innocuous inquiry as to the identity of a person,” the judge observed, adding that its “obvious insinuation” was that there could be more than one man who could be described as the child’s father.The case dates back to March 23, 2021, when Priyanka Gupta was walking with her three-year-old daughter near RBI Enclave Gate in Paschim Vihar. As the child cried, Gupta told her, “Dekho papa aa gaye, don’t cry.” Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected, “Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”Gupta initially ignored the remark and, about two minutes later, handed over the child to her husband after he arrived in a car. She later informed her father-in-law, who called the police, following which an FIR was registered at Paschim Vihar East police station under Section 509 IPC.In his statement under Section 313 CrPC, Lal admitted making the remark but claimed it was not made with any “ill intention”. He also alleged false implication, with the defence arguing that Gupta wanted him removed from the street corner where he had run his ironing business for seven years.Rejecting the defence, the court observed: “The explanation offered by the accused that the words were spoken without ‘ill intention’ is a bare assertion. No surrounding circumstance has been brought on record from which the remark could reasonably acquire an innocent meaning.”The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC, as the insult must have the requisite nexus with her modesty. In this case, however, it held that the remark was personally directed at Gupta and made immediately after she referred to her child’s father, carrying a sexually derogatory insinuation concerning her relationship with men and the child’s paternity.The court held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and convicted Lal under Section 509 IPC.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
articles.summary: Bombay High Court orders X to remove a video targeting Serum Institute and CEO Adar Poonawalla; issues show-cause notices for alleged defiance of injunction.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order. Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Cornell case spotlights 'confusing' web of systems for reporting campus assaults
articles.summary: Victims often have to navigate both university and local law enforcement processes to find justice.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of sexual assault.

When Mary was a first-year college student, she woke up after a fraternity party with bruises and bite marks all over her body. She says it took her a few days to piece together that she had been sexually assaulted while "blacked out", and to find the strength - and the right avenue - to report the assault.

The man she accused was eventually expelled, but police declined to bring charges because they said there was a lack of physical evidence.

Mary - whose name has been changed to protect her identity - says the process of finding some measure of justice was oftentimes confusing and disappointing.

"Even though it was a positive outcome, it was still so emotionally exhausting and draining, because I had to do all of this in tandem with getting used to being a college student for the first time," said Mary. "In many ways, I had to be my own advocate, gathering all my evidence."

The experience with local police, she added, "left me with a deep sense of disappointment in the system".

How both universities and the criminal justice system respond to these types of assaults on college campuses is once again under the spotlight, after a former student at Cornell University filed a civil lawsuit alleging she was raped by several members of a fraternity two years ago, with prosecutors declining at the time to pursue a case.

Mary did not attend Cornell, and her case is not connected with the university. But advocates for survivors of sexual assault say her case, and the Cornell allegations, are emblematic of the larger challenges in responding to sexual assault claims on college campuses specifically.

The confusing web of systems and policies - which varies greatly by college - is one of several reasons why the vast majority of sexual assaults on college campuses, research suggests, go unreported.

"These processes are hard to navigate if you aren't in trauma," said Nancy Chi Cantalupo, an associate professor of law at Wayne State University who has represented victims on college campuses. "If you are in trauma, they're virtually impossible to navigate."

Earlier this month, the former Cornell student known only as Jane Doe filed a lawsuit against the Ivy League university, alleging she was drugged and raped by several men at a fraternity house at the university in 2024.

She also alleged that Cornell failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved. Jane Doe said she had reported the alleged assault to campus police, who interviewed her, and provided information to the district attorney's office. The prosecutor declined to bring charges at the time, but this week, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten re-opened the case.

Both Cornell and Van Houten have defended their handling of the 2024 case. I n a statement , the university said it had "conducted an extensive investigation and adjudication over several months and imposed different sanctions based on the findings and circumstances involving each student" in addition to creating a new framework for addressing sexual assault on campus.

Cornell has said it followed the procedures outlined in a federal civil rights law called Title IX. The law mandates that universities follow certain rules about investigating sexual assaults. Cornell said its investigation resulted in the fraternity involved being barred from campus, and that students involved were suspended or expelled.

Typically, after a student reports an assault on campus, the university's Title IX office determines whether the alleged behaviour could constitute a violation of policy.

Eventually, both parties attend a hearing with a panel of faculty members or other mediators to present evidence and testimony in the case before a decision by the school is reached.

One of the biggest challenges sexual assault survivors face is simultaneously navigating the university and the criminal justice system, which "serve different purposes, operate under different rules and timelines, and lead to different outcomes", said Zoey Scheinblum-Brewer, a policy coordinator at the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network, a nonprofit anti-sexual assault organisation.

"Unclear guidance about the options available through these parallel processes can create so much confusion and uncertainty that some students ultimately decide not to report," she said.

Mary said this process at her college was not clear to her when she made the decision to report the assault.

"For me, it would've been nice to know what I was getting into before it all happened. It felt like they were learning the process alongside me," she said of university officials.

While some colleges, like Cornell, have information sharing agreements with local police, Mary was told she had to go to police separately to file a report - a process she found physically exhausting.

Mary's lawyer says there was surveillance footage from the night showing her alleged rapist carrying her "slumped" over, and she had pictures of her bruises and bite marks. But police told Mary they did not have probable cause for an arrest, and that the district attorney wanted to leave it to university administration.

"I was left with this taste that because they knew that the college was 'handling' my investigation, that they could wipe their hands clean of it," she said.

The local police department told the BBC it did not have the details of this particular case. The local district attorney's office did not respond to a request for comment.

University investigations are done behind closed doors, said Helene Weiss, a lawyer who has represented several victims of sexual assault on college campuses. She believes that part of the reason for the secrecy is to protect institutions' reputations.

"The secrecy of the process, it prevents other students from knowing about it. It prevents witnesses from coming forward," she said.

Michael Diamondstein, a Pennsylvania attorney who has represented those accused of sexual misconduct on college campuses, said the secrecy helps protect both the victim and the accused.

"I think when you compare it to what they would face in a courtroom, it's much easier for students and much safer for students. Their name isn't put out there. The news media doesn't get them," he said.

Cornell students have criticised the university's handling of the woman's claims. The Cornell Daily Sun, a student newspaper, published the names of the accused under the headline: "Cornell won't, we will."

In a statement, the college said that federal privacy law "prohibits Cornell from disclosing specific information regarding individual students" so it cannot "make a public statement on any other disciplinary response".

Many advocates say there is merit to universities investigating sexual assault complaints separately from the criminal justice system. Prosecuting sexual assault cases is notoriously difficult - a recent systematic review found that less than 10% of sexual assault cases yielded convictions. In a criminal trial, a prosecutor must convince a jury "beyond reasonable doubt" that the accused is guilty. But in a campus tribunal, the burden of proof is lower.

Under Title IX, the university is also required to offer solutions that local law enforcement cannot, like ensuring a student is not in the same class as their alleged abuser while the investigation is ongoing and offering homework extensions, said Scheinblum-Brewer.

This is one of several reasons why victims and advocates for survivors say there are benefits to having two separate avenues, through the university and the criminal justice system.

For Mary, after her case was dropped by the police, pursuing her assault claim through Title IX became the only way for her alleged rapist to face repercussions: an expulsion from college.

"This was my only avenue to achieve any sort of justice," she said.

articles.title: Esteticista reage a assalto e recupera celular em Ribeirão Preto | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima foi abordada por dupla em bicicleta na noite de terça-feira (29) no Jardim Califórnia, em Ribeirão Preto. Imagens de câmeras de segurança registraram toda a ação.
articles.summary: Após ser abordada no Jardim Califórnia, esteticista reage a assalto em Ribeirão Preto e recupera celular e objetos de trabalho após perseguição.
articles.body:
Uma esteticista que reagiu a um assalto, correu atrás do ladrão e conseguiu recuperar o aparelho celular em Ribeirão Preto (SP) relata que ganhou forças para agir ao pensar no prejuízo e no transtorno que teria se os criminosos levassem tudo que estava na bolsa dela.

O crime foi cometido na noite de terça-feira (29) em uma avenida no Jardim Califórnia, Zona Sul da cidade. Durante a ação, até uma criança que estava próxima correu atrás de um dos assaltantes. Ninguém foi preso.

Os ladrões levaram a bolsa e R$ 200 que estavam no interior dela, mas outros objetos como a chave de casa da vítima, remédios e o celular caíram durante o confronto e foram recuperados pela vítima.

"Hoje o celular tem muitos dados pessoais, eu trabalho com o público, então acaba que eu tenho uma agenda que eu tenho que seguir, eu tenho o material do meu trabalho. Na hora que eu comecei a pensar em tudo que eu ia perder, tudo que ia ficar na mão deles, foi a hora que eu tive força, que eu falei assim, não dá, não pode, não vai dar", disse a vítima, que preferiu não ser identificada.

Esteticista reage a roubo, corre atrás de ladrão e recupera celular em Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/ Câmeras de segurança

Eram por volta de 19h quando a esteticista chegou ao endereço, onde participaria de um curso de artesanato. Ela desceu do carro e logo observou a aproximação de dois homens em uma bicicleta.

"Foi tudo muito rápido, né? Eu desço do carro, vou ao porta-mala, pego os nossos materiais de trabalho que estavam ali e chego a fechar o porta-mala e vou para a calçada. No momento que eu estou na calçada, eu me viro e vejo que um daqueles meninos que estavam de bicicleta estava atrás de mim", lembra.

Segundo ela, um deles se aproximou a pé e foi direto em direção à bolsa que estava com a vítima, que não se acuou.

"Ele veio em direção mesmo a mim, com aquele rosto de quem ia me fazer mal mesmo. E nesse momento eu já comecei a gritar e a reagir."

A esteticista conta que continuou a segurar a bolsa, mesmo com os puxões do assaltante, e o acompanhou pela avenida, até quando caiu no canteiro central.

"A minha bolsa estava bem presa ao meu ombro, então foi o tempo que deu segurar, e a gente foi se arrastando até o canteiro central da avenida. Ali, na verdade, eu nem sei o que aconteceu, eu imagino que foi a hora que a alça da minha bolsa arrebentou, que foi a hora que eu vi que eu não ia ter mais como segurar."

Pelas imagens de câmeras de segurança, depois disso, esse criminoso fugiu, assim como um comparsa que estava de bicicleta, e que chegou a ser perseguido por uma criança que estava correndo.

Como a bolsa ficou aberta durante toda a ação, alguns objetos acabaram caindo no canteiro central. A vítima conta que somente descobriu quando conseguiu acessar remotamente a geolocalização do aparelho celular.

"Eu vi que estava dando a localização de onde eu estava e coloquei para fazer um sinal sonoro. Foi a hora que eu corri para o canteiro, ouvi o barulho e achei o celular. Na hora que eu achei o celular eu pensei 'tem mais coisa'. (...) A gente conseguiu recuperar meu óculos, o medicamento que eu tomo, que é um pouquinho caro, a gente conseguiu recuperar as chaves da minha casa."

articles.title: Montes Claros investe na iluminação pública | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura leva mais luz para os quatro cantos da cidade.
articles.summary: Prefeitura leva mais luz para os quatro cantos da cidade.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Montes Claros, através da Empresa Municipal de Serviços, Obras e Urbanização (ESURB), está empenhada em aprimorar a iluminação urbana em toda a cidade, seja por meio da expansão da rede ou pela manutenção dos espaços já iluminados. Esses esforços abrangem não apenas ruas e avenidas, mas também quadras e praças.

Recentemente, as intervenções foram direcionadas para os bairros Santo Amaro, Santa Rafaela e Vila Telma. Esses locais ganharam novas luminárias e receberam troca de lâmpadas, ampliando assim a cobertura da iluminação pública, fundamental para a segurança urbana, já que ambientes bem iluminados oferecem maior sensação de proteção e desestimulam atividades ilegais.

A serviço da Prefeitura de Montes Claros, a Empresa Municipal de Serviços, Obras e Urbanização (ESURB) atua diariamente na manutenção da iluminação pública nas avenidas, ruas, praças, parques, quadras esportivas e campos de futebol, tanto na área urbana quanto na zona rural do município.

Além das trocas de lâmpadas, quando tecnologias antigas são substituídas por outras mais modernas e eficientes, a ESURB realiza a instalação de pontos de energia nas feiras livres dos bairros, atendendo ao programa CONECTA MOC, tornando a cidade cada vez mais inteligente e inclusiva.

articles.title: Produtora de microgreens e flores comestíveis expande negócio em Teresópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Crédito para construção de estufas ajudou produtora a ampliar a produção e gerar empregos no campo.
articles.summary: Crédito para construção de estufas ajudou produtora a ampliar a produção e gerar empregos no campo.
articles.body:
Investimentos na construção de estufas permitiram expandir a produção e fortalecer o desenvolvimento da propriedade rural — Foto: Sicredi/Divulgação

A busca por inovação e diferenciação no agronegócio tem impulsionado produtores rurais da Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro a investir em novos modelos de negócio. Em Teresópolis, a produtora rural Maria Lúcia Nogueira, da localidade de Morro Agudo, encontrou no Sicredi um parceiro para ampliar a produção de cultivos especializados e fortalecer o crescimento da propriedade.

Ao lado da família, a produtora trabalha com flores comestíveis, cogumelos e microgreens, produtos que atendem mercados específicos e exigem cuidados diferenciados no cultivo. Desde o início da atividade, o desafio era investir continuamente em melhorias que permitissem aumentar a produtividade e garantir a qualidade da produção ao longo de todo o ano.

Uma das principais necessidades da propriedade era a ampliação das estufas agrícolas. Por se tratar de um cultivo que depende de ambiente protegido, especialmente durante períodos de chuva, a estrutura se tornou fundamental para viabilizar a expansão do negócio e reduzir os impactos climáticos sobre a produção.

Foi por meio do acesso ao crédito que a família conseguiu investir na construção das estufas e ampliar gradativamente sua capacidade produtiva. O que começou em pequena escala evoluiu ao longo dos anos, permitindo o crescimento da operação e a abertura de novas oportunidades para o empreendimento rural.

Com a expansão da produção, a propriedade também passou a gerar mais empregos na comunidade. Atualmente, o negócio emprega 17 pessoas, em sua maioria mulheres, que atuam em atividades como colheita, processamento e embalagem dos produtos cultivados na fazenda.

Segundo a produtora, além dos recursos para investimento, a proximidade no atendimento foi um dos fatores que fizeram diferença durante a jornada de crescimento. O processo de abertura de conta e contratação do crédito aconteceu de forma simplificada, diretamente na propriedade, reduzindo deslocamentos e facilitando o acesso às soluções financeiras.

Diretamente na propriedade, Maria Lúcia contou com um atendimento próximo e facilitado para acessar o financiamento e ampliar sua produção de microgreens — Foto: Sicredi/Divulgação

A história de Maria Lúcia Nogueira reflete uma realidade presente em muitas propriedades da Região Serrana: produtores que buscam inovar, agregar valor à produção e gerar desenvolvimento local, mas que precisam de apoio para transformar projetos em resultados.

Ao ampliar sua presença na região, o Sicredi reforça seu compromisso de apoiar produtores rurais de diferentes perfis e tamanhos, oferecendo soluções adequadas às necessidades de cada negócio. Além de disponibilizar crédito, o Sicredi aposta em um relacionamento próximo para entender a realidade de quem está no campo e contribuir para a construção de uma agricultura cada vez mais forte, sustentável e próspera.

O Sicredi é uma instituição financeira que em 2027 completará 125 anos de história, mais de 10,5 milhões de associados e presença em todo o Brasil. Com mais de 3.100 mil agências, oferece mais de 300 produtos e serviços financeiros para pessoas, empresas e o agronegócio, atuando com um modelo que valoriza o relacionamento próximo, a participação dos associados e o desenvolvimento das regiões onde está presente.

articles.title: Christa Pike sobrevive a injeção letal; ela seria a primeira mulher executada no Tennesse em 200 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Os advogados de Pike, que matou uma colega estudante em 1995, afirmam que ela deveria receber clemência e não seria condenada à morte se o crime acontecesse hoje.
articles.summary: Os advogados de Pike, que matou uma colega estudante em 1995, afirmam que ela deveria receber clemência e não seria condenada à morte se o crime acontecesse hoje.
articles.body:
Christa Pike em 12 de janeiro de 2023. — Foto: TDOC via AP

As autoridades do Tennessee não conseguiram executar Christa Gail Pike nesta quarta-feira (30) por um assassinato cometido em 1995, mesmo após a administração de duas doses de um medicamento letal. Um especialista em pena de morte afirmou que se trata de uma falha sem precedentes.

Pike permaneceu viva e roncando alto após a tentativa de execução por injeção letal e foi retirada da prisão em uma ambulância, segundo seus advogados.

“Não fomos informados sobre seu estado de saúde”, disseram os advogados de Pike em comunicado.

Pike, de 50 anos, estava programada para ser executada às 10h de quarta-feira pelo assassinato que cometeu aos 18 anos e seria a primeira mulher executada no Tennessee em mais de 200 anos. Um tribunal de apelações suspendeu a injeção letal apenas uma hora antes do horário previsto, mas horas depois a Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos derrubou a suspensão.

Segundo os advogados, as autoridades administraram duas doses de pentobarbital em Pike. Robin M. Maher, diretora-executiva do Death Penalty Information Center, afirmou que o que ocorreu com Pike é “algo único e sem paralelo”.

Ela disse que outras sete pessoas sobreviveram a problemas médicos decorrentes da incapacidade das equipes de execução de acessar uma veia para administrar os medicamentos, mas que ninguém havia permanecido vivo após receber as drogas usadas nas execuções.

“Não sentimos satisfação em estar certos, mas as preocupações levantadas pela sra. Pike se mostraram verdadeiras: acesso venoso difícil, veias rompidas, pentobarbital degradado, ausência de atendimento médico de emergência quando as coisas inevitavelmente dão errado, tudo isso sob um protocolo que continua envolto em sigilo.”

Testemunhas descreveram o processo de execução

Testemunhas da imprensa que observavam a execução de uma sala separada disseram que as autoridades abriram as cortinas da câmara de execução às 19h27, mostrando Pike presa a uma maca.

Pike permaneceu acordada e, em determinado momento, levantou a cabeça e perguntou aos funcionários da prisão se seu braço deveria estar se sentindo daquela forma. Não ficou claro a que ela se referia.

Às 20h26, testemunhas relataram que a segunda dose de pentobarbital havia sido administrada.

Veículos de emergência chegam à Instituição de Segurança Máxima de Riverbend após a execução de Christa Pike ter sido interrompida na quarta-feira, 30 de setembro de 2026, em Nashville, Tennessee. — Foto: George Walker IV / AP

Pike continuou sendo ouvida roncando atrás da cortina fechada até que o microfone foi desligado às 20h53. Nesse momento, foi anunciado que as testemunhas da imprensa seriam escoltadas para fora da área.

A porta-voz do Departamento de Correções do Tennessee, Dorinda Carter, disse às testemunhas que não tinha informações imediatas sobre o que havia ocorrido.

Os advogados de Pike apresentaram ainda na noite de quarta-feira um pedido emergencial à Suprema Corte dos EUA para interromper imediatamente a execução, alegando que ela estava sofrendo uma “agonia desnecessária” e que seu direito de não ser submetida a punições cruéis e incomuns estava sendo violado.

Eles também protocolaram pedidos no Tribunal de Apelações do Sexto Circuito e em um tribunal distrital.

O recurso também afirmava que o Departamento de Correções deveria iniciar medidas para salvar a vida da condenada.

“A falha em fornecer esse atendimento constitui indiferença deliberada diante de necessidades médicas legítimas e graves”, diz a petição.

Pessoas contra a pena de morte rezaram em frente à Instituição de Segurança Máxima de Riverbend antes da execução planejada de Christa Pike. — Foto: George Walker IV / AP

Pike e seu namorado foram condenados pelo esfaqueamento e espancamento que matou Colleen Slemmer, de 19 anos, colega deles em uma instituição de treinamento profissional em Knoxville, em 1995. O caso ganhou ampla repercussão porque um pentagrama gravado no corpo da vítima e outros elementos do crime alimentaram temores sobre cultos satânicos durante o chamado “pânico satânico” das décadas de 1980 e 1990.

Foi a segunda vez neste ano que o Tennessee não conseguiu realizar uma execução. Em maio, autoridades cancelaram a injeção letal de Tony Carruthers após os executores passarem mais de uma hora tentando, sem sucesso, conseguir acesso intravenoso para administrar o pentobarbital.

Suspensão da execução foi rapidamente contestada

Inicialmente, Pike seria executada pela manhã. As testemunhas já estavam reunidas na prisão de segurança máxima Riverbend, em Nashville, quando o Tribunal de Apelações do Sexto Circuito decidiu por 2 votos a 1 suspender a execução.

O tribunal afirmou que era necessário mais tempo para analisar se as alegações de abuso sexual na infância apresentadas por Pike haviam sido plenamente consideradas durante sua condenação.

O gabinete do procurador-geral recorreu à Suprema Corte, argumentando que a suspensão de última hora traumatizou a família da vítima e recompensou “táticas abusivas de atraso” dos advogados da condenada.

Mais tarde, a Suprema Corte autorizou que a execução prosseguisse. A maioria conservadora não explicou sua decisão, enquanto os três integrantes da ala liberal registraram voto divergente afirmando que as alegações de Pike mereciam uma análise mais aprofundada.

Pike não nega ter cometido o assassinato, mas seus apoiadores argumentam que o estado deveria considerar sua idade na época do crime, suas doenças mentais e suas alegações de abuso sexual severo.

“É inconcebível que, no século 21, o sistema de Justiça criminal esteja prestes a executar uma sobrevivente de estupro e abuso sexual infantil cujo júri jamais teve a oportunidade de considerar esses fatos ao avaliar sua responsabilidade moral”, escreveram seus advogados.

Caso reacendeu debate sobre pena de morte para jovens

À medida que a data da execução se aproximava, o debate sobre a pena de morte para jovens infratores voltou a ganhar força.

O defensor público federal adjunto Stephen Ferrell afirmou que a sentença de morte de Pike é uma exceção, já que outras condenações de jovens de 18 anos no Tennessee foram posteriormente anuladas.

Após o crime, Pike foi diagnosticada com transtorno bipolar e transtorno de estresse pós-traumático. Em seu pedido de clemência, afirmou que pretendia apenas brigar com Slemmer, mas acabou matando a jovem durante um ataque de fúria.

“Eu era uma jovem de 18 anos com doença mental. Levei muitos anos para compreender a gravidade do que havia feito. Ainda mais para aceitar quantas vidas afetei. Tirei a vida do filho, da irmã e da amiga de alguém. Hoje me enoja pensar que fui capaz de cometer um crime desses”, disse Pike em declaração.

Mãe da vítima diz que espera cumprimento da sentença

A mãe de Slemmer afirmou que deseja que a execução seja realizada e disse que espera há décadas pelo cumprimento da sentença.

“Toda vez que penso nisso, penso em Colleen sentindo aquela dor e tentando se levantar e correr”, disse May Martinez à Associated Press.

Martinez afirmou que um grupo arrecadou dinheiro para que ela e o marido pudessem viajar da Flórida ao Tennessee para testemunhar a execução.

“Não há um dia sequer, nem um minuto, em que eu não pense em Colleen. Os feriados são os piores”, disse ela, observando que a filha teria completado 51 anos em setembro.

O crime abalou a cidade de Knoxville. Segundo os promotores, Pike, temendo que Slemmer estivesse tentando roubar seu namorado, atraiu a jovem para uma área de mata em 12 de janeiro de 1995. Ela cortou Slemmer com um estilete e a espancou com um grande pedaço de asfalto. Shipp, namorado de Pike, admitiu que foi ele quem gravou um pentagrama no corpo da vítima.

Shipp tinha 17 anos quando o crime ocorreu e recebeu prisão perpétua com possibilidade de liberdade condicional. Pike foi a única condenada à morte.

Desde que a Suprema Corte restabeleceu a pena de morte em 1976, 18 mulheres foram executadas nos Estados Unidos , o equivalente a cerca de 1% de todas as execuções, segundo o Death Penalty Information Center.

Pike teria sido a 30ª pessoa executada nos Estados Unidos neste ano, após a execução realizada na Flórida na terça-feira.

Em 2024, o Tennessee anunciou que substituiria o protocolo de três drogas usado em injeções letais por um método baseado apenas no pentobarbital. A mudança ocorreu mais de dois anos depois de o estado interromper abruptamente a execução de Oscar Smith e reconhecer que não havia garantido a testagem adequada dos medicamentos utilizados nas execuções.

articles.body:
Empreendedor ampliou a atuação da empresa após investimentos realizados com apoio do Sicredi — Foto: Sicredi/Divulgação

Em um cenário cada vez mais competitivo para o comércio local, investir em melhorias e encontrar novas oportunidades de crescimento é um dos principais desafios enfrentados por pequenos empreendedores. Em Teresópolis, o empresário Roicer Pereira encontrou no Sicredi o apoio necessário para modernizar sua empresa, ampliar sua atuação no mercado e fortalecer seu negócio.

Proprietário de uma loja voltada principalmente para a comercialização de cestas básicas, Roicer Pereira buscava alternativas para se adaptar às mudanças do mercado e manter a competitividade da empresa. Foi nesse momento que iniciou seu relacionamento com o Sicredi, a partir de uma visita da equipe da cooperativa para conhecer de perto a realidade do negócio.

Segundo o empresário, o trabalho começou com um diagnóstico sobre as necessidades da empresa, incluindo a análise do perfil dos clientes, das oportunidades de crescimento e das soluções mais adequadas para o momento vivido pelo empreendimento. A partir desse acompanhamento, foram estruturadas alternativas para apoiar a expansão do negócio.

Com o acesso às soluções da cooperativa, o empreendedor conseguiu reformar a loja e investir na aquisição de um veículo utilizado para o transporte de mercadorias. A melhoria da logística permitiu ampliar o atendimento aos clientes e aumentar a capacidade operacional da empresa. Além disso, um novo projeto já está em andamento para a aquisição de um caminhão de pequeno porte, com o objetivo de dar suporte à próxima etapa de crescimento.

Os investimentos também possibilitaram a diversificação do portfólio. Além das cestas básicas, a loja passou a oferecer itens de utilidades domésticas, ampliando as opções disponíveis para os consumidores e criando novas oportunidades de receita. A expectativa do empresário é continuar expandindo a operação com novas categorias de produtos nos próximos anos.

Com soluções financeiras adequadas à realidade da empresa, o empreendedor ganhou mais praticidade para vender e atender seus clientes — Foto: Sicredi/Divulgação

Outro fator que contribuiu para a evolução do negócio foi a adoção de soluções financeiras voltadas ao dia a dia da empresa. Com a utilização da máquina de cartões e das ferramentas digitais disponibilizadas pelo Sicredi, a loja passou a oferecer diferentes formas de pagamento, incluindo Pix, débito, crédito e links de cobrança, facilitando as vendas e ampliando as possibilidades de atendimento ao cliente.

A trajetória de Roicer Pereira representa a realidade de muitos empreendedores da Região Serrana que buscam parceiros capazes de compreender seus desafios e construir soluções alinhadas aos seus objetivos. Mais do que oferecer produtos financeiros, o Sicredi atua de forma próxima aos associados, acompanhando suas necessidades e apoiando o desenvolvimento sustentável dos negócios.

Com expansão na Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro, a cooperativa reforça seu compromisso de impulsionar o crescimento de empresas de diferentes segmentos e portes. Ao combinar relacionamento, orientação e soluções financeiras personalizadas, o Sicredi contribui para que empreendedores transformem projetos em resultados e fortaleçam a economia das comunidades onde atuam.

O Sicredi é uma instituição financeira que em 2027 completará 125 anos de história, mais de 10,5 milhões de associados e presença em todo o Brasil. Com mais de 3.100 mil agências, oferece mais de 300 produtos e serviços financeiros para pessoas, empresas e o agronegócio, atuando com um modelo que valoriza o relacionamento próximo, a participação dos associados e o desenvolvimento das regiões onde está presente.

articles.title: Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss
articles.summary: Scientists say such rapid melting is no longer surprising given the pace of climate change.
articles.body:
Swiss glaciers have suffered a near-record loss of ice in 2026, new data shows, as intense summer heatwaves take their toll on Alpine peaks.

More than 5% of the country's remaining glacier ice has disappeared in the last 12 months, which scientists say is "extraordinary".

They warn that such rapid melting is no longer a surprise given the pace of climate change, but it could threaten water supplies for farming, hydropower and transport in the decades ahead.

The loss of glacier ice can also destabilise mountain slopes and increase the risk of landslides in some places - which can lead to flash flooding in extreme cases, as seen in Nepal in August.

There were multiple factors involved in that event, which was triggered when a large area of bedrock and glacier ice collapsed.

But scientists say long-term glacier thinning and the thawing of frozen ground likely raised the risks.

The notable finding from this latest report is not so much that Swiss glaciers are shrinking - which is to be expected in our warming climate, driven primarily by fossil fuel emissions - but the sheer pace of melting.

Until recently, glaciologists in the Alps considered 2% of ice lost in a single year to be "extreme". This year has seen an estimated 5.5% disappear.

"It's really just disastrous," said Dr Matthias Huss, director of Glacier Monitoring Switzerland, which produced the report.

Swiss glaciers started the summer in an already difficult place, covered by less snow than usual after a mild winter.

And much of that snow disappeared quickly in the early and intense heatwaves of May and June , exposing the glacier ice below.

Bare ice is darker and less reflective than fresh snow, so absorbs more of the Sun's energy.

That left glaciers vulnerable to melting even faster in subsequent heatwaves.

"Ten years ago, I wouldn't have thought that it's possible to lose glaciers so quickly," said Dr Fabien Maussion, a glaciologist at the University of Bristol, who was not involved in the Swiss report.

"What's happened over the summer now is extremely distressing… but at the same time it was to be expected from a climate scientist's perspective," he added.

Meltwater from glaciers can be an important source of water for irrigation, hydropower and even shipping traffic during hot, dry conditions.

Scientists estimate that Swiss glaciers released 2.2 trillion litres of meltwater between July and September.

Although that helped to ease water shortages this summer, it has rapidly diminished the frozen supply.

The loss of ice could pose long-term challenges, Huss warned, with smaller glaciers unable to top up water levels to the same extent.

"Every drop of water that runs off during these heatwaves is kind of old water that's been stocked in the glacier ice centuries or decades ago," said Huss.

"It's helping us [now] but it's unsustainable, so we won't have it at [our] disposal in the next heatwave."

The River Rhine reached record lows in places this summer , affecting shipping navigation routes and increasing transport costs.

One of the most ominous findings is what researchers observed at measurement sites at the highest elevations, where temperatures are lowest and glaciers are typically snow-covered.

Even as high as 3,500 metres above sea level, scientists found no snow remaining at the end of summer.

"At some glaciers we've seen four metres of ice loss at the highest point, where they should be covered by several metres of winter snow at this time of the year," said Huss, from Glacier Monitoring Switzerland.

Snow is like glacier food - and under stable conditions some of it would eventually compact into ice.

But if no snow survives the summer, it cannot replace the ice lost to melting at lower, warmer elevations. The glacier will starve, shrink and eventually disappear.

"Glaciers are complex because they gain mass at the top and they flow downstream, so there is a lot of physics," explained Maussion.

"But in its simplest form, what we see right now is that we took an ice cube out of the fridge and it's just melting in front of our eyes."

Scientists say the climate is now too warm for many Alpine glaciers to survive.

Some, like Plattalva in eastern Switzerland, have already disappeared.

But researchers stress that sharp cuts to carbon emissions can still save much of the world's glacier ice.

This is particularly the case for the Himalayas and the polar regions, where most of the planet's ice resides.

"There we still can make a big difference with protecting the climate," said Huss.

"If these ice masses can be saved or stabilised, we can limit the rise of global sea levels… which could affect billions of people living along the coast."

articles.title: Georgia college student miraculously survives 8-story plunge after metal bench breaks her fall
articles.summary: A University of Georgia student fell eight stories at Rambler Athens after dancing near an open window, but a metal bench may have broken her fall.
articles.body: A 21-year-old University of Georgia student survived an eight-story fall from an apartment window after apparently falling through a screen while dancing near an open window, according to a police report obtained by Fox News Digital. Kristin Sargent fell from an eighth-floor window at the Rambler Athens apartment complex on West Broad Street around 7:37 p.m. Saturday. Witnesses told police Sargent had been dancing on a couch or air mattress near the open window when she apparently fell through the screen. She landed near a pool in a courtyard on the building's second floor, according to the report. Police found evidence that Sargent struck a metal bench during the fall. An officer noted blood on the bench's cushion and that one of its armrests had broken off. WOMAN DIES AFTER PLUNGING INTO UNCOVERED MANHOLE OUTSIDE LUXURY STORES Lt. Katie Jenkins, a spokesperson for the Athens-Clarke County Police Department, told Fox News Digital that investigators believe the bench helped break Sargent's fall. She said the incident is not being investigated as a criminal matter and that police understand Sargent is alert and conscious. Emergency 911 audio obtained by FOX 5 Atlanta captured the frantic moments after Sargent fell. "We’re on the eighth floor. My friend just fell out of the window," a caller told dispatchers. "She's on the ground. She fell out of the window. We were dancing, and she just fell out of the window." A dispatcher asked whether Sargent was moving. MAN ACCUSED OF LURING UGA STUDENT WITH ‘WALK HOME’ RUSE BEFORE BRUTAL ASSAULT: POLICE "Is she moving? Is she moving? No, she's not," the caller responded. The caller later told the dispatcher she could see Sargent below but could not determine whether her eyes were open. "No, I don't know. I'm looking down at her on the floor. She's not moving," the caller said. Emergency responders transported Sargent to a hospital, where police investigators interviewed her and witnesses while forensic personnel investigated, according to the police report. LAKEN RILEY MURDER EXPOSED GLARING SECURITY LAPSES ON COLLEGE CAMPUSES, NEED FOR EMERGENCY BLUE LIGHTS A responding officer wrote that information gathered at the time suggested the fall was an accident. Jenkins told Fox News Digital police are not investigating the incident as a criminal matter. The report identifies Sargent as a resident of the apartment where the fall occurred. Police could not address the window or what safety measures may or may not have been in place. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Rambler Athens previously said it was reviewing the incident. Fox News Digital reached out to the apartment complex for additional information about the window and any safety measures in place at the time of the fall. A representative for the University of Georgia did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for additional information.

articles.title: Indonesia is building a school from residual plastic waste; even its floors, ceilings, pipes and frames will use discarded plastic
articles.summary: Bakti Barito is constructing what it describes as Indonesia's first school from residual plastic waste with the material used not only for bricks but also
articles.body: Bakti Barito is constructing what it describes as Indonesia's first school from residual plastic waste with the material used not only for bricks but also for floor panels, ceilings, roofs, pipes, and window and door frames. Bakti Barito, the philanthropic foundation of Barito Pacific Group, marked the groundbreaking on 12 June 2026 for the new SDN 3 Sukanegla building in Garut Regency. The project will transform approximately 15 tons of residual plastic waste into two classrooms and two toilet units. According to the Bakti Barito Foundation official press release, it targets low-value plastics, such as instant noodle wrappers and sachets, that have no economic value in the recycling market. The foundation had planned to inaugurate the school in July 2026, at the start of the new academic year.How is Indonesia building a school from residual plastic wasteThe foundation says plastic waste is used not only for the bricks but for all structural elements. It says every one of these components uses plastic waste. These include floor panels, ceilings and roofs, as well as pipes, window frames and door frames. Every one of these components uses plastic waste.The foundation says the project will transform approximately 15 tons of residual plastic waste into two classrooms and two toilet units for the children at the school. It adds that the school's construction is targeted for completion within a few weeks. According to the foundation's June announcement, the inauguration was planned for July 2026, at the start of the new Academic Year.What type of residual plastic waste is the initiative targetingThe initiative focuses on low-value residual plastics, which Bakti Barito identifies as the type of plastic waste accumulating most in local landfills (TPA). It distinguishes these from PET (Polyethylene Terephthalate), widely used for bottled drinks, PP (Polypropylene), widely used for food and beverage containers, and HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene), widely used for shampoo bottles and jerrycans packaging.Residual plastics such as instant noodle wrappers and sachets, the foundation says, have no economic value in the recycling market. As a result, this waste is routinely ignored by scavengers and informal sector workers, because it cannot be resold to commercial recycling plants. Bakti Barito states that by creating an alternative use for this neglected waste, the project diverts tons of plastic waste from the ecosystem and opens a new chapter in the circular economy.What did Fifi Pangestu say about Indonesia’s plastic waste initiativeFifi Pangestu, Executive Director of Bakti Barito, said during her remarks that environmental innovations must bring positive impacts and tangible benefits directly to local residents. She also appreciated the courage of the Garut Regency Government in pioneering the adoption of this solution. She described the plastic waste challenge as an opportunity to build something valuable for future generations, and said the collaboration of local governments and technology partners shows that residual plastics can be part of the solution by providing spaces for children to learn while helping to reduce the burden on the environment. articles.title: Reparations advocates slam cash compensation ‘handout’ label, point to past government remedies
articles.summary: Reparations advocates demand direct cash payments to descendants of enslaved Americans, warning broader eligibility risks are diluting the movement.
articles.body: Reparations advocates are insisting that the federal government provide direct cash payments to Black descendants of American slavery, warning that broadening the eligibility scope risks diluting the movement amid growing resistance from conservatives and the Trump administration. "Cash payments — that’s just a little solution to it, but it’s a big solution because without cash payments, there’s no reparations," Rev. Phyllis Coachman, a supporter of the U.S. Freedmen Project, told Fox News Digital. "[Slavery] ended in 1865, but so many other things happened after that," Coachman added. "After slavery, the collapse of Reconstruction. We had Jim Crow. We had legal segregation, disenfranchisement. We had lynching "We had racial terror, destruction of Black property and communities, housing discrimination, redlining, discriminatory lending, barriers to wealth building …. the war on drugs and mass incarceration." CHAOS ERUPTS AT NY REPARATIONS HEARING AS ‘FOUNDATIONAL’ BLACK AMERICANS CLASH WITH LEFT-LEANING GROUPS The U.S. Freedmen Project, an organization representing self-identified "foundational Black Americans," works to educate the public on the distinctions between Black Americans who are direct descendants of enslaved persons in the U.S. and those who immigrated to the country voluntarily. According to its official website, the group is a nonpartisan organization seeking to fulfill the abandoned missions of the 19th-century Freedmen’s Bureau and the Freedmen’s Savings and Trust Company. Supporters argue that broader reparations bills risk violating constitutional principles, contending instead that state and federal officials must base eligibility criteria strictly on lineage. The debate comes as several state and local governments explore reparations initiatives intended to compensate Black residents for historic racial injustice. Evanston, Illinois, a Chicago suburb, became the first U.S. city to offer direct remedies, providing up to $25,000 in homeownership grants and cash payments to eligible Black residents to address legacy housing discrimination. Reparations advocate Annette Wilcox pushed back against critics who frame direct monetary payouts as government handouts, arguing the term is used selectively to delegitimize Black claims. "My thoughts about people who say cash payments are handouts is this is a government that has given trillions of dollars to all sorts of people as reparations," Wilcox told Fox News Digital. "We have reparations for 9/11. We've had — even things that aren't reparations after the crash and the Depression, there was an estimated $5 trillion in programs, money and remedies given to people — 90% went to White people at that time. So, handouts are, you know, just, frankly, an insult that people give to Black people. "The government has a responsibility for what it did to the citizens — the Black people who were enslaved in this country — and it needs to own up to it just like it owned up to what it did to the Native Americans, the Japanese and many other groups that it has given reparations to." SOME BLACK NEW YORKERS DEMAND CASH PAYMENTS AS ONLY 'TRUE' FORM OF JUSTICE Fox News Digital previously attended a public hearing hosted by the New York State Community Commission on Reparations Remedies at Hempstead High School on Long Island. During the hearing, residents warned panel officials that expanding the definition of reparations to include recent immigrants or other marginalized groups risks co-opting the movement. The New York commission was established after Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation in December 2023 creating a state panel to examine the legacy of slavery in New York and evaluate potential remedies. Among those who testified in Long Island, U.S. Freedmen movement supporter Aubrey Muhammad called for an explicit payout amount of $800,000 per eligible individual. "We need $800,000 for each foundational Black American. That's simple," Muhammad told Fox News Digital. "In New York, that's about the cost of living that'll get you a home, a small business, or help you recover from financial duress." CHICAGO SUBURB LOCALS HOPE REPARATIONS ADDRESSES 'AFFORDABILITY PRESSURES' AS BLACK POPULATION DWINDLES However, Devine Prince, president of the U.S. Freedmen Project, noted that such figures reflect broader efforts to address the national wealth gap rather than standard baseline figures. Still, Prince maintained that direct compensation remains non-negotiable. "That needs to be repaired through direct monetary compensation to American freedmen."

articles.title: Austria's Semmering Railway, completed in 1854 across 41 kilometres of mountains with tunnels and viaducts, still carries trains 172 years later
articles.summary: Infrastructure is built to last, and few are as striking as the Semmering Railway in Austria.
articles.body: Infrastructure is built to last, and few are as striking as the Semmering Railway in Austria. Constructed between 1848 and 1854 over 41 kilometres of high mountains, it was one of the greatest feats of civil engineering from the pioneering age of railways. Its tunnels, viaducts and other works were built so well that the line has stayed in continuous use ever since. In 2026, more than 170 years after completion, engineers finished the main renovation work on its largest viaduct, and regular trains are running again. The old stonework and modern upkeep show how heritage can keep working.Where the Semmering Railway runs: From Gloggnitz to MürzzuschlagUNESCO notes the line begins at Gloggnitz station in Lower Austria, 436 metres above sea level, and climbs for 29 kilometres to its highest point at the pass, 895 metres up. It then descends for a further 12 kilometres to Mürzzuschlag station in Styria, at 677 metres. Along the way, it passes through a series of tunnels and viaducts, including the Klamm Tunnel, the Schwarza viaduct and the two-storey curving viaduct over the Kalte Rinne, before the 1,431-metre Semmering Tunnel leads to Semmering station. The World Heritage Centre describes the last section as the most dramatic of the route. The inscribed property covers 156 hectares, surrounded by a buffer zone of 8,581 hectares.The engineering that made the Semmering Railway a feat of civil engineeringThe line's fourteen tunnels are 1,477 metres long in total, nearly one-tenth of the route, and its sixteen major viaducts also add up to 1,477 metres. There are 118 smaller arched stone bridges and eleven iron bridges. Most tunnel portals are simple but monumental, with varied ornamentation, and the support structures are largely stone, with brick used for the viaduct arches and tunnel linings. Fifty-seven two-storey attendants' houses stand at roughly 700-metre intervals, a characteristic feature of the line. According to the World Heritage Centre, the continued operation of the line testifies to the engineering genius of project engineer Carl von Ghega.Why the Semmering Railway is a World Heritage site, it has been in continuous use since 1854The railway was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 1998 for two reasons. First, it represents an outstanding technological solution to a major physical problem in early railway construction. Second, it opened areas of great natural beauty to residential and recreational use, creating a new form of landscape. The Semmering Pass became one of the first purpose-built Alpine resorts, known for the summer architecture of its villas and hotels. The line's appearance changed when overhead wire poles were erected between 1957 and 1959 for electric locomotives. Federal protection has applied since 1923, and a management plan has been in place since 2008.How Austrian Federal Railways keeps the Semmering line running until the base tunnel opensKeeping a line this old running takes constant work. According to Austrian Federal Railways, about two and a half months of work, chiefly to renovate the Kalte Rinne viaduct, ended on 29 May 2026, when normal traffic resumed. Crews renewed the reinforcement with around 92 tonnes of steel, laid roughly 1,200 square metres of waterproofing, and renewed 200 metres of track; the company is investing about twenty million euros this year. Trains kept running on one track from 14 March to 28 May. The operator says the mountain line will stay vital until the Semmering Base Tunnel opens at the end of 2029.You use AI every day. articles.title: Japan raises permanent residency fees for foreign nationals by twenty-fold
articles.summary: The hikes are part of immigration policy changes introduced to manage Japan's growing foreign population.
articles.body:
Japan has raised fees for foreigners looking to reside in the country, with the cost of permanent residency going up 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955).

Those seeking permanent residency must now also meet new income, pension and Japanese-language requirements.

Long lines formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants sought to beat the fee hikes, with Tokyo's main immigration bureau reporting wait times of over seven hours.

The fee increases are part of a series of changes to Japan's immigration policy under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, which aim to manage its rapidly growing foreign population.

In July, Japan implemented a five-fold increase in visa fees for all foreigners – its first visa fee hike in 50 years. Authorities said this was meant to "reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations".

Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive in Japan, the nation's ageing population is increasingly relying on foreign workers to plug a labour shortage.

Japan's foreign resident population surpassed 4.12 million at the end of 2025, marking a record 9.5% increase from the previous year. This however has led to growing anxieties over immigration and social change.

Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her key priorities since she took office in October last year.

In an X post days before the residency permit hikes set in, Takaichi wrote that her government recognises that "some members of the public may feel a sense of concern or unfairness" as Japan's foreign resident population grows.

"To address these concerns, [the government] is working to ensure that its policies toward foreign nationals are orderly, and that both Japanese citizens and foreign residents can live safely and securely," she wrote.

Before the hikes, it would cost non-permanent residents in Japan 6,000 yen each time they applied to change their residency status or extend their period of stay.

From 1 October, the fee varies according to the duration of stay sought – from 10,000 yen for three months or less, to 75,000 yen for five years or more.

Applicants who face financial hardship or are designated as refugees would be granted discounts.

Aspiring permanent residents must now also earn a stable income at or above the Japanese average. Latest data released in July puts average household income at 5.75 million yen as of 2024.

Micaiah Michaela-Spence, who has been living and working in Tokyo for 10 years, was not able to compile the necessary documentation to submit his application for permanent residency before the price hike.

The 37-year-old still plans to apply, but questions the new measures aimed at foreign residents.

"My immediate reaction was that foreigners were being treated a bit too conveniently. We're being asked to make more than the average Japanese person, pay a significantly higher fee, just to be able to work in Japan and provide taxes," he tells the BBC.

"There's already a significant language and cultural barrier that prevents some talent from coming over. This just doesn't strike me as a plan that was thought out to the long term."

From April next year, permanent residency applicants will face even tighter requirements, including basic Japanese language proficiency. This has led to a surge in enrollments at Japanese language schools as well as people signing up to take the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test, local media reported.

Applicants' expected pension benefits must also be equivalent to that of someone who has enrolled into the employee pension system for 30 years, although the value of one's financial assets can be considered if their expected pension benefits fall short.

articles.title: Woman convicted of killing 10-year-old held in Delhi after 20 years in hiding
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence. A life convict in a kidnapping-murder case of a 10-year-old boy, Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005.Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar.The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point. Police said witnesses Jagdish Chand and Vasdev had seen Sadhana holding his hand while crossing GT Road around 5.30pm. Sadhana and co-accused Raj Kumar were arrested from Jahangirpuri.The two were living together and the child’s father, Balwant Ram, and his family had objected to it. A previous dispute led to resentment and a decision to take revenge, police said.During the trial, Sadhana was found to be the last person seen with the child. Police said she had also concealed Kumar’s presence at her house and played an active role in the conspiracy. She was convicted under sections 302 (murder), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment. Sadhana was lodged in Tihar Jail on Jan 9, 1990.After spending years in jail, Sadhana was released on parole on Dec 27, 2005, which was extended by three weeks on medical grounds. She, however, did not surrender on Jan 18, 2006, and began a second life.She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. Police said her final parole was arranged by another Raj Kumar, a Tilak Nagar resident, on the reference of Janki, a woman who was lodged with Sadhana in jail. Sadhana stayed with him before taking up a job at a private company in Noida.There, she met Keshav, a carpenter. They moved to Mukundpur, where they lived for around five years before shifting to Haridwar. Police said Sadhana married Keshav in a temple and used his name as her husband in documents, helping conceal her identity.Meanwhile, investigators continued to pursue leads through intelligence, old associates and family links. A recent lead about a woman living under an assumed identity took a team to Haridwar and Sadhana was arrested on Sept 27. articles.title: Christa Pike’s execution by lethal injection fails in Tennessee
articles.summary: Witnesses say Tennessee officials were unable to execute Christa Pike after a lethal injection attempt.
articles.body:
Officials in the United States have failed to put a Tennessee woman to death for a murder she committed in 1995, after the lethal injection was halted for hours as courts considered a last-minute appeal to stay her execution.

Christa Gail Pike, 50, had been scheduled to die on Wednesday for a killing she committed at age 18, after the US Supreme Court overturned an appeals court ruling that stopped the lethal injection just an hour before it was to start.

Her death would have been Tennessee’s first execution of a woman in at least 200 years.

Following the top court’s ruling, officials attempted to go ahead with the execution as planned and appeared to give Pike two doses of the sedative pentobarbital, according to media witnesses.

At 7:46pm local time (23:46 GMT), prison officials closed the curtain separating Pike from the media viewing room. It was raised three minutes later, when witnesses said Pike could be heard loudly snoring.

The curtain was closed again at 8:06pm. Witnesses continued to hear Pike snoring until the microphone was switched off at about 8:53pm, when they were told to leave the area. Emergency vehicles were seen coming and going from the prison.

The Tennessee Department of Correction did not immediately explain why the execution had not been completed.

Pike had initially been scheduled to die on Wednesday morning , and witnesses had already gathered at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville when the 6th Circuit US Court of Appeals voted 2-1 to issue a stay.

The appeals court said a delay was needed to consider whether Pike’s allegations of childhood sexual abuse were fully considered during her sentencing.

Later on Wednesday, the Supreme Court cleared the way for the execution to proceed. Its conservative majority did not explain the decision, while the three liberal justices dissented. Justice Sonia Sotomayor wrote that vacating the stay “unnecessarily prevents” the appeals court from giving due consideration to Pike’s claim.

Tennessee’s attorney general had argued that delaying the execution traumatised the family of Pike’s victim, Colleen Slemmer, and rewarded what it called “abusive delay tactics”.

Pike and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, were convicted of the fatal stabbing and beating in 1995 of 19-year-old Slemmer, their classmate at a job training facility in Knoxville.

Shipp was 17 when the crime happened and received a sentence of life in prison with the possibility of parole. Pike was the only one sentenced to death.

Pike does not deny committing the killing, but her supporters argue the state should consider her age at the time, her mental illness and her allegations of severe sexual abuse, including that she was raped from early childhood.

“It is inconceivable that in the 21st century, the criminal justice system is poised to execute a survivor of rape and child sexual abuse whose jury never had the opportunity to consider those facts in weighing the defendant’s moral culpability,” her lawyers wrote in a filing.

After the killing, Pike was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.

In her clemency petition, she said she had initially intended to fight Slemmer but killed her in a frenzied attack when she could not “put the brakes on”.

“I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realise the gravity of what I’d done. Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone’s child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime,” Pike said in a statement.

Slemmer’s mother has said she wants Pike’s death sentence carried out after waiting decades for the execution.

Tennessee has not executed a woman for at least 200 years, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Since the Supreme Court reinstated the death penalty in 1976, 18 women have been executed in the US, representing about 1 percent of all executions, according to the centre.

articles.body: Israeli authorities are investigating the midair crisis on a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv after a co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and attempted to take control of the aircraft.The incident is being probed as a possible attempted terrorist attack, while the alleged attacker, an Omani national, has been taken into custody by Saudi authorities. Israeli authorities have said they were investigating whether the incident constituted an attempted terror attack, while the motive had not been immediately established.The Daily Mail also reported that a source described as a colleague expressed regret over the airline’s decision to have the man on the flight, saying the incident had nearly resulted in the deaths of those onboard. The report quoted the source as questioning how the Omani national had been assigned to a flight bound for Israel.14,000ft plunge before passengers intervenedThe confrontation began while the aircraft was cruising towards Israel. articles.title: Arizona sheriff's helicopter crew rescues man stranded atop overturned truck in rapidly rising floodwaters
articles.summary: Video captures a Maricopa County sheriff's helicopter crew hoisting a man from his overturned truck as flash flooding surged in Tonopah, Arizona.
articles.body: Dramatic video shows an Arizona sheriff's helicopter crew rescuing a man stranded on top of his overturned truck as rapidly moving floodwaters surrounded the vehicle. The Maricopa County Sheriff's Office said its Fox 1 aviation crew responded Tuesday morning to a flooded wash in Tonopah, where deputies found the man sitting atop the overturned vehicle with water rushing around him. Video released by authorities shows the man perched on the truck as muddy floodwaters rush past him. Because of the dangerous conditions, first responders determined that directly reaching the man was too risky and decided a "hoist rescue" would be the safest option. TRAGEDY AT SEA LEAVES TEEN STRANDED ON OVERTURNED BOAT FOR NEARLY 3 DAYS IN FRIGID WATERS A member of the Fox 1 crew is seen being lowered toward the vehicle before securing the man in a rescue harness and being hoisted to safety with him. The man was taken to the riverbank, where fire personnel were waiting, according to the sheriff's office. The helicopter's pilot, Rich Dickner, told CBS News that the water was quickly rising around the vehicle. "We didn't waste much time," Dickner said. "As opposed to when we first got there, you can see the water line on the video — it's below the window — and it had risen up to the top of the window," he continued. "So there was that urgency." HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF People reported that Deputy Lindsey Smith was lowered approximately 80 feet from the helicopter toward the overturned truck.
